description: Plan: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.57.html (revision 2), ticket 1. Every dispatch plan's shared Fail node is the arm of last resort and records the exception it stands for, set by the construct that built the plan: function heads/guards -> FunctionClauseError naming M.f/arity; = -> MatchError with the value; case -> CaseClauseError with the value; cond -> CondClauseError; with/else -> WithClauseError with the value; receive has no Fail. Interp, run and build lower every Fail through one named panic route that prints '** (Name) message' as Elixir prints an uncaught exception, with one exit status; it is what becomes raise. Kernel's panic(:badarith) and other library failures use the same route. Today: native halt_with_atom(:function_clause|:match_error) (jobs/native.rs ~104/420/461/2894), the interpreter's own 'function_clause: no backend entry clause matched' (ir_interp/backend.rs:663), Kernel panic(:badarith). The value renders with the dbg rendering until fz-sc8.10 inspect lands. Tests compare exception name, message and exit status with elixir's stderr on all three paths. The page's ticket-1 section is completed from the failure-route inventory before building.
title: Every decision ends in an arm of last resort that names its exception
